priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 2, 3, and 4; handoff section 8 weak uncertainty calibration / excessive abstention. This experiment builds directly on the graded abstention-release result (Partially demonstrated, 2026-11-03): all seven criteria PASSed on the additional cohort, and its failures were criterion 6 (PRIMARY) and criterion 4 on the development cohort. Criterion 4's failure is recorded in that grading as INHERITED from the carried return-A profile (the candidate was identical to its decisive baseline at return-A onset) and is carried here unchanged as a co-graded guard, not as this cycle's target. This cycle's selected limitation is the criterion-6 failure: ONE stationary control state (checkpoint 8, seed 392039) at which an opposed pair SURVIVED both release-gate legs at the gate's MINIMUM corroboration - realized reference purity 0.857 (leg P armed by design on stationary evidence) and acting_opposed_count exactly 3, i.e. supporting_opposed_count exactly 1 (leg S satisfied at its lowest admitted value) - and the candidate abstained on all 16 tasks there (0 successes / 0 harm against recent8's 7 / 9), costing the entire control successes deficit (118 vs recent8 125, required at least 119; FAIL by 1). The same gate blocked the development cohort's only other stationary trigger by leg S alone (control checkpoint 8, seed 392003, purity 0.857, acting_opposed_count 2) and went 0/240 abstentions on the additional cohort, so at its current bar the gate is a thinner lottery, not a property of the branch. This cycle changes exactly one thing: it raises leg S of the abstention release gate - and only that leg, on only that branch - from acting_opposed_count >= 3 to acting_opposed_count >= 4, i.e. the triggering pair must be corroborated by at least TWO further opposed events among the 6 acting-window events preceding it. The graded abstention-release protocol's own threshold arithmetic pre-warned that this bar cuts checkpoint-2 onset retention to roughly 0.18 (matched-adjusted), so the trade - stationary survival down by roughly a factor of three per triggered state, onset abstention retention down to roughly 0.41-0.55 pooled for leg S alone - is itself the hypothesis, graded on both sides. This cycle's headline criterion is therefore again criterion 6, stationary-control selectivity, graded as PRIMARY; criterion 5 (release by checkpoint 32, including the zero-abstention sub-condition (d) the preceding cycle added and PASSed on both cohorts) and criteria 1, 3, and 4 (the onset harm profiles the thinned abstention helps protect) are the co-graded guards the higher bar must not give back.
capability_under_test: Stationary abstention survival at the release gate's minimum corroboration: whether raising the abstention release gate's support leg to at least two supporting opposed events (acting_opposed_count >= 4) can close stationary survival (control successes at least recent8 - 6, control harm at or below recent8, control abstentions at most 32 of 240, per cohort) without thinning onset abstention past the onset harm margins (criteria 1, 3, and 4 at their carried levels) and without giving back the graded checkpoint-32 release (criterion 5, including abstained branch in 0 of 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states) - against recent8, cumulative, frozen_A, the evidence-opposition guard, and the reference-purity and abstention-release candidates as baselines, the abstention-release candidate being the decisive comparison (identical but for the support threshold: >= 3 there, >= 4 here). Priority 1 items 2 + 3 + 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 weak uncertainty calibration and excessive abstention.
hypothesis: The graded abstention-release records localize the remaining stationary failure to the support leg's MINIMUM, not to the gate's structure: the one surviving stationary state satisfied leg S at exactly its lowest admitted value (acting_opposed_count 3, one supporting event), while the cohort's other stationary trigger was blocked by leg S alone at acting_opposed_count 2, and the additional cohort drew no surviving stationary trigger at all. Leg P cannot help here by construction - on stationary evidence the reference window is segment-pure (design purity 0.8375; the surviving state realized 0.857) - so the only observed-stream quantity that separated the surviving state from a blocked one is the support count itself. Raising leg S to acting_opposed_count >= 4 (at least two supporting opposed events among the 6 preceding acting-window events) moves the bar one step: a stationary trigger now survives leg S with probability P(at least 2 opposed among 6 own-rule events) = about 0.25 raw (per-event opposed probability 0.1625) and about 0.18 matched-adjusted (0.13) - down from about 0.65 / 0.57 at the >= 3 bar, roughly a threefold cut per triggered stationary state. The cost side is pre-computed with the same rates and is the reason this is a hypothesis rather than a fix: at checkpoint-2 onset the 6 preceding acting-window events are previous-segment (own-rule relative to the reference majority), so checkpoint-2 onset retention under leg S alone falls to the same 0.18-0.25; at checkpoint-4 onset (2 current-rule + 4 previous-rule among the 6) retention is about 0.84 raw / 0.65 adjusted; pooled onset retention for leg S alone is therefore about 0.55 raw / 0.41 adjusted, and combined with leg P at its onset design arming (about 0.95; realized 1.00 across pooled onset states on both graded purity cohorts and armed at every B2 onset state in the graded abstention-release cohorts) about 0.39-0.52 of the reference-purity candidate's onset abstentions survive - against the graded abstention-release candidate's own pooled onset abstentions of 16/288 (development) and 32/288 (additional), and against criterion-3 margins of 30 (development: candidate 160 vs guard 190) and 30 (additional: 148 vs 178) pooled harm on those cohorts, with the preceding cycle's one realized leg-S disarming at onset costing +15 pooled harm on development. An unlucky draw under the higher bar can therefore fail criteria 1, 3, or 4 even as criterion 6 passes; both directions are graded, neither is excused. Late checkpoint-32 survival also tightens: leg P's realized arming at checkpoint-32 states was 6/9 (development) and 4/9 (additional) in the graded abstention-release experiment, and leg S survival there is the own-rule figure 0.18-0.25, giving roughly 0.08-0.17 per triggered late state (the preceding cycle realized zero late abstentions on both cohorts, one of them by active disarming under both legs; criterion 5(d) is carried at 0 of 9 so any regression is charged). Two honest limits are pre-registered, not hidden: (1) a flipped pair on stationary evidence is LOCALLY IDENTICAL to a genuine onset pair - the newest events, the acting window, the local window, the reference, and the archive have the same distributions in the two cases - so no observed-stream condition can separate them individually; this cycle does not claim to identify the cause of a pair, it raises a calibrated evidence bar one further step and grades the quantified trade on both sides. A stationary trigger that draws two supporting opposed events still fires a full 16-task abstention, and if it does, criterion 6 is charged exactly as before. (2) The onset-retention arithmetic is computed from the published noise rates and segment geometry alone; realized span sparsity (events on spans absent from the reference are unmatched, not opposed) can thin onset retention below these figures, as pre-registered in the preceding protocols, and that thinning is charged through criteria 1, 3, and 4, not excused.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 together are the pooled onset window for criteria 1, 2, 3, and 4; 32 grades release (criterion 5, with its new abstention sub-condition) and is part of the stationary population for criterion 6 (this experiment's PRIMARY criterion); 8 and 16 report persistence costs, including the abstention gate's leg trajectories (realized purity against the design values and realized acting-window opposed counts). Checkpoint values are benchmark bookkeeping only: the learner never receives k, a stage name, or any elapsed-since-switch count (see permitted_observations); the reference purity, the acting-window opposed count (with its raised support threshold of 4), and all windows are fixed observed-stream summaries, not segment measurements - the design values by checkpoint are consequences of the published segment geometry acting on those summaries, not inputs to the learner. Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world.

simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures gate selectivity when nothing changed - false recovery, false minority engagement, false abstention, lost productivity - and is this experiment's PRIMARY population: the graded purity failure occurred here (one full abstention at control checkpoint 32) and the graded abstention-release failure occurred here (one full abstention at control checkpoint 8 surviving both gate legs at minimum corroboration), the reference window never mixes segments on this arm (design purity the pure-segment level 0.8375 at every control checkpoint, so leg P is designed armed throughout and leg S is the only leg that can release a stationary abstention), and the acting window is single-segment throughout.

permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, checkpoint value, stage position, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its signals, its concordance tests, its minority set or minority fraction, its authority condition, its reference purity, its acting-window opposition count, its recovery models, or its checkpoint record. In particular the abstention release gate is computed from reported events, their spans, the extended reference window's own per-span majorities, and the last 8 observed events only: the learner has no access to how many events have elapsed since any switch, to which events belonged to any segment, or to whether any segment exists - the purity fraction and the acting-window opposed count are fixed observed-stream summaries, not segment or switch detectors fed with privileged boundaries.

training_indices.control_A_continuation: 5000..5063 (64 episodes, physics original, stationary control arm only)

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).

candidate.name: AbstentionHigherCorroborationRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory, EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory, BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory, LongDisagreementJointRecoveryMemory, ExtendedReferenceJointRecoveryMemory, MinorityArchiveJointRecoveryMemory, ReferencePurityGatedRecoveryMemory, and AbstentionReleaseGatedRecoveryMemory are baselines in this experiment, not modified by it.

fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard, retained-recovery, joint, bounded, long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned: for each of the newest 2 events, a hard span-majority expectation over the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-52 .. N-3); strictly-highest reported class wins, tie or empty gives null; an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different; opposed_count in 0..2; no fitted probabilities anywhere. The decision record ALSO carries the legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only, never a decision input), exactly as in the graded candidates, so the graded long candidate's rule remains derivable from the records alone.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: every observed event BEFORE the original reference partition, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. Not phase-segmented, not a snapshot, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full. Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference) on the SAME event. joint_count in 0..2.
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.authority_condition: IDENTICAL to the graded long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned - all three legs, computed from the observed reported stream only, using the same span-majority machinery: (A) LOCAL-ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (local window = last 26 events; stable_disagreement iff comparable C >= 1 AND disagreeing D satisfies D * 2 > C); (B) ACTING-WINDOW ARCHIVE CONCORDANCE (recent_concordant_count = archive-concordant events among the last 8, in 0..8); (C) PRECEDING-WINDOW ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (preceding window = 26 events immediately before the local window; preceding_stable_disagreement iff C2 >= 1 AND D2 * 2 > C2; long_disagreement iff stable_disagreement AND preceding_stable_disagreement). BRANCH AUTHORITY for the carried-over branches, unchanged: ABSTENTION armed (before the new release gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement; RECOVERY armed (before the carried-over purity gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement OR recent_concordant_count >= 2 OR long_disagreement. Would-have-fired disarmed branches are recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire) and fall through. The release gate carried over from the graded abstention-release candidate is an ADDITIONAL condition on the abstention branch only (see abstention_release_gate); it does not modify any leg of this condition, and this condition does not enter the gate's computations beyond the abstention arming it already supplied. No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters either condition.
fixed_parameters.minority_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded minority-archive and reference-purity candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned. Computed from the retained archive (events[:N-26]) and its own per-span majorities only. For each archive event e: let M(e) be the archive expectation for span(e) under the unchanged archive concordance definition (strictly-highest reported class among archive events of that span; tie or empty gives null). e is ARCHIVE-MATCHED if M(e) is progress or damage AND e's reported class is progress or damage. e is MINORITY (discordant) if archive-matched AND e's reported class DIFFERS from M(e). The MINORITY SET is the set of all minority archive events, in chronological order. minority_matched_count (over the archive) = number of archive-matched archive events; minority_discordant_count = size of the minority set; minority_fraction = minority_discordant_count / minority_matched_count (0 if minority_matched_count == 0). All three counts and the fraction are recorded at every checkpoint.
fixed_parameters.minority_arming: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: the minority branch is ARMED (before the carried-over purity gate) iff minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8. When the branch is not armed it cannot be taken, whatever the minority joint count says; a would-have-fired disarmed minority branch is recorded (minority_would_fire) and falls through.
fixed_parameters.minority_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the MINORITY EXPECTATION for span(e) is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among MINORITY-SET events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is MINORITY-MATCHED if its minority expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is MINORITY-CONCORDANT if minority-matched and its reported class EQUALS the minority expectation. minority_concordant_count and minority_matched_count (over the newest window) are in 0..2 and are recorded in full, with per-event minority records exactly as in the graded candidates.
fixed_parameters.minority_joint_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is MINORITY-JOINT if it is MINORITY-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference, unchanged) - both flags on the SAME event. minority_joint_count in 0..2, recorded in full with per-event minority joint flags.
fixed_parameters.minority_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the MINORITY SET events only, with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.reference_purity_gate: CARRIED OVER IDENTICALLY from the graded reference-purity candidate, unchanged and not re-tuned, and applied to the two RECOVERY branches exactly as graded there. Computed from the extended reference window (the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window, indices N-52 .. N-3 - the SAME window the immediate signal reads) and its own per-span majorities only. For each reference event e: let R(e) be the reference expectation for span(e), i.e. the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among REFERENCE events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is REFERENCE-MATCHED if R(e) is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is REFERENCE-CONCORDANT if reference-matched AND e's reported class EQUALS R(e). reference_matched_count and reference_concordant_count are over the 50 reference events; reference_purity = reference_concordant_count / reference_matched_count (0 if reference_matched_count == 0). The purity gate is ARMED iff reference_purity >= 0.70. Regular recovery fires iff joint_count >= 1 AND the carried-over recovery authority is armed AND the purity gate is armed; minority recovery fires iff minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed AND the purity gate is armed (and regular recovery did not fire, per the decision order). A recovery trigger blocked by purity alone is recorded (recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity) and falls through. In the graded abstention-release experiment the same purity quantity and threshold additionally entered the abstention branch through its release gate - as leg P of that gate, with the quantity, its window, and its threshold all unchanged; that gate is carried over here identically except for its leg-S threshold (see abstention_release_gate).
fixed_parameters.abstention_release_gate: CARRIED OVER from the graded AbstentionReleaseGatedRecoveryMemory with exactly ONE changed quantity: the leg-S support threshold is raised from 3 to 4. A release gate on the ABSTENTION branch only; the recovery branches, their authority condition, the purity gate as applied to them, the minority branch, the acting model, and every carried-over definition are unchanged. The abstention branch fires iff ALL of the following hold: (i) the carried-over trigger and arming hold (opposed_count == 2 AND abstention authority armed, i.e. NOT stable_disagreement); (ii) LEG P - the reference-purity gate is armed (reference_purity >= 0.70, the identical quantity and threshold that bound the recovery branches, UNCHANGED); and (iii) LEG S (RAISED) - ACTING-WINDOW OPPOSITION SUPPORT: acting_opposed_count >= 4, where acting_opposed_count is the number of opposed events among the LAST 8 observed events, each of those 8 events scored against the SAME extended-reference per-span majorities used by the immediate signal (an acting-window event is matched / opposed under the identical hard span-majority definition: expectation = strictly-highest reported class among the 50 reference events of that span, tie or empty gives null; matched iff expectation and reported class are both progress or damage; opposed iff matched and different). The newest 2 events are the last 2 of the acting window, so acting_opposed_count includes the triggering pair: whenever the trigger holds (opposed_count == 2), leg S is equivalently the requirement that at least TWO of the 6 acting-window events preceding the newest window are also opposed (supporting_opposed_count = acting_opposed_count - opposed_count >= 2). An abstention trigger whose carried-over arming holds but which the release gate blocks is recorded and falls through to recent8: abstention_disarmed_by_purity is true iff leg P alone blocked it (purity disarmed, leg S satisfied), abstention_disarmed_by_support is true iff leg S alone blocked it (support count below the raised threshold, purity armed), and both flags are true iff both legs blocked it; both flags are FALSE when the carried-over authority was already disarmed (the release gate did not block that state - the authority did, exactly as in the graded candidates) and when the branch is taken. All gate quantities are recorded at every checkpoint: the per-event acting-window opposition records for all 8 acting-window events (span, reference-set event count for that span, reference majority class or null, reported class, matched flag, opposed flag), acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, the support threshold (4 in this experiment), purity_armed (already recorded with the purity record), abstention_gate_armed (the conjunction of legs P and S), and the two disarmed flags. No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters the computation: both legs are fixed observed-stream summaries of windows this candidate family already computes (the 50-event reference window and the 8-event acting window). THE SINGLE NEW ELEMENT OF THIS EXPERIMENT is the raised leg-S threshold (4 in place of the graded candidate's 3); every other element of the gate, and of the candidate, is identical to the graded abstention-release candidate.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1 AND the recovery branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive), exactly as the graded reference-purity candidate. (2) MINORITY RECOVERY - else if minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed (minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the minority model (source recorded as minority_archive), exactly as the graded reference-purity candidate. (3) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2 AND the abstention branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the abstention release gate is armed (leg P purity armed AND leg S acting_opposed_count >= 4, the raised threshold), abstain (choose returns None). (4) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. A branch whose trigger fires while the branch is disarmed - by its own arming, by the carried-over authority, by the purity gate, or (abstention only) by the release gate's support leg - is recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire, plus recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity where purity alone blocked a recovery branch, and abstention_disarmed_by_purity / abstention_disarmed_by_support where the release gate blocked abstention) and falls through. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: The graded abstention-release cycle gave the abstention branch the same treatment the recovery branches received - an evidence-derived release gate (leg P reference purity plus leg S acting-window corroboration at >= 3) - and it removed abstention from the checkpoint-32 records on both cohorts while preserving the onset profile on the additional cohort exactly and on development at one absorbed disarming. Its one stationary failure survived at leg S's minimum: a single supporting opposed event. This cycle therefore changes the minimal possible thing: the support threshold moves one step, from one supporting event to two - the same style of minimal corroboration step the family has used throughout (the recovery authority's corroboration leg requires at least 2 archive-concordant events among the last 8) - and grades the trade the preceding protocol itself priced: checkpoint-2 onset retention falls to about 0.18-0.25 under this bar, so if stationary selectivity is restored only by deleting the branch's onset protection, criteria 1, 3, and 4 will show it and the cycle fails on that side instead. The design deliberately does NOT re-threshold any other carried-over count (the purity threshold stays at 0.70, the abstention trigger stays at opposed_count == 2, leg P stays identical), and it deliberately does NOT claim the raised bar identifies WHY a pair is opposed: on stationary evidence a flipped pair is locally identical to an onset pair (pre-registered in the hypothesis), so the gate remains a calibrated evidence bar with a quantified onset cost, graded on both sides - not a switch detector.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates: the extended signal (and with it the reference purity and the acting-window opposition count, which read the same 50-event reference window) requires a 2-event newest window and a full 50-event reference window (at least 52 observed events); the archive concordance test requires at least 27. Below 52 events the extended signal, the purity gate, and the abstention release gate are not evaluable, reference_purity is recorded as 0 with purity_armed false and the per-event purity records empty, the acting-window opposition records are empty with acting_opposed_count and supporting_opposed_count recorded as 0 and abstention_gate_armed false, joint_count and minority_joint_count are recorded as 0 (their opposed side is not evaluable), and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable, gate_evaluable false). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so all windows are full and the fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record - per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events, acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity and abstention_disarmed_by_support flags - all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates, the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records, and this simulator's published segment geometry, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). (i) SUPPORT THRESHOLD acting_opposed_count >= 4 (THE SINGLE NEW PARAMETER VALUE): one step above the graded abstention-release candidate's >= 3 - the trigger itself contributes exactly 2 opposed events (the newest window), so the raised threshold requires exactly TWO further opposed events among the 6 preceding acting-window events. The graded abstention-release protocol considered this value and rejected it there because its checkpoint-2 retention cost (about 0.18 matched-adjusted) would delete most of the branch's then-unproven onset protection; the graded outcome since recorded - the branch's onset profile preserved on both cohorts at >= 3, its sole stationary failure surviving at exactly the >= 3 minimum - is the published evidence that reopens the question as an experiment, not as a re-tune: no parameter was adjusted against the graded cohorts' scores to make those cohorts pass; the new bar is tested on NEW cohorts and graded against margins it is pre-computed to threaten. Retention arithmetic from the composed rates (per-event opposed probability about 0.1625 raw / 0.13 matched-adjusted against an own-rule majority; about 0.8375 raw / 0.67 adjusted against an opposite-rule majority): stationary and checkpoint-2 onset states (6 preceding acting-window events all of the reference's own rule) retain with probability 1 - (1-p)^6 - 6p(1-p)^5 = 0.253 raw / 0.178 adjusted; checkpoint-4 onset states (2 opposite-rule + 4 own-rule among the 6) retain with probability 0.843 raw / 0.647 adjusted; pooled onset retention (checkpoints 2 and 4 equally weighted) about 0.548 raw / 0.412 adjusted for leg S alone, and about 0.39-0.52 combined with leg P at its onset design arming (about 0.95; realized 1.00 across pooled onset states on both graded purity cohorts). Stationary survival per triggered state falls from the >= 3 bar's 0.655 raw / 0.566 adjusted to 0.253 raw / 0.178 adjusted. Late checkpoint-32 survival: leg P armed share realized 6/9 (development) and 4/9 (additional) in the graded abstention-release experiment times leg-S survival about 0.18-0.25 gives about 0.08-0.17 per triggered late state. (ii) PURITY THRESHOLD 0.70: carried over UNCHANGED from the graded reference-purity protocol, as applied to the recovery branches there and to the abstention branch (as leg P) in the graded abstention-release protocol - the identical quantity, window (50 events), and threshold. It is not re-derived and not re-tuned here. (iii) All other carried-over thresholds are UNCHANGED and not re-tuned: newest window 2, extended reference 50, legacy reference 24, archive events[:N-26], local window 26, preceding window 26, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention trigger opposed_count == 2, strict-majority rule D * 2 > C in both authority windows, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2, minority fraction threshold 0.25, minority count floor 8, minority joint threshold 1, purity threshold 0.70. The only changed fixed parameter in this experiment is the abstention gate's support threshold, 4 in place of 3.

expected_failure_modes: Stationary false pair surviving both legs (pre-registered, the cycle's central risk): leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; the graded failure state realized 0.886) and does not release stationary abstention at all; leg S releases a stationary trigger only when none of the 6 preceding acting-window events is opposed (probability about 0.34-0.43 per triggered state). A stationary opposed pair WITH one supporting opposed event among the preceding 6 therefore still fires a full 16-task abstention, and a single such state at a control checkpoint where recent8 scores about 10 or more is by itself likely to fail criterion 6's successes sub-condition (margin 6) unless offset by productive control recovery elsewhere, exactly as the development cohort of the graded purity experiment was offset (+6 from one control recovery) and the additional cohort was not. This outcome is charged against criterion 6, not excused, and the report must state the surviving state's realized purity, acting_opposed_count, and supporting count.

Onset abstention thinning costing the harm guards (pre-registered): the gate retains only about 0.72-0.78 of the reference-purity candidate's pooled onset abstentions by design - the lost firings are concentrated at checkpoint 2 (retention about 0.57-0.66 there) and at B1 onset, where abstention is the family's only protective response (recovery is archive-discordant-blocked and the minority branch is unarmed there by design). Each lost firing returns 16 tasks to recent8 play at onset harm rates of roughly 8-14 per state; against the graded purity margins (criterion 3: 58 / 85 pooled harm below the guard; criterion 1(c) B2: 16 / 29 below the guard; criterion 4: 42 / 25 below the guard) a typical draw is designed to pass, but an unlucky cohort - several lost B1 firings, or lost firings concentrated in one cell - can fail criterion 3's per-cell sub-condition (at least 5 of 6 cells at or below recent8 becomes easier, not harder, when abstention is lost, since recent8 play equals recent8 harm; the binding risk is the guard comparison in criterion 3(a) and criteria 1(c) / 4) and is charged, not excused. Realized gate disarmings are recorded at every onset state (split by leg), so a thinning failure is fully distinguishable from a trigger failure in the report.

Late abstention surviving the gate at checkpoint 32 (pre-registered): leg P's realized checkpoint-32 arming on the graded purity cohorts was 3 of 9 states per cohort (self-fit compression raised realized purity to 0.645-0.810 against the 0.5675 global design value), so a late state with purity at or above 0.70 AND a supporting opposed event (combined survival about 0.19-0.22 per triggered state) still takes the abstained branch and fails criterion 5's new sub-condition (d) (0 of 9 abstained states) even while sub-conditions (a)-(c) pass. That outcome would show the release gate's late leg is too weak on realized (self-fitted) purity values, and would redirect the next cycle toward an expiry summary that is not self-fitted, under its own new protocol - the same redirect the purity protocol pre-registered for its own failure mode 2.

Purity leg disarming onset abstention on purity noise (pre-registered, smaller than in the purity experiment because abstention is a thinner branch): the checkpoint-4 design purity is 0.8105, about 1.6 sd above the 0.70 threshold at roughly 40 matched reference events, so on an unlucky cohort an onset state can realize purity below 0.70 and lose an abstention firing the reference-purity candidate would have taken (its recovery branches faced the same risk in the graded experiment and realized zero onset disarmings on both cohorts; abstention states are fewer, so the expected count is lower, but any realized onset purity disarming is recorded and charged against criteria 1, 3, and 4 through the lost protection).

Support-count span sparsity: the acting-window opposition records score 8 events against reference majorities fitted on about 5-6 events per span; on spans absent from the reference the expectation is null and the event is unmatched (not opposed), so acting_opposed_count can read low on thin-span draws at ANY checkpoint, including genuine onset states - a further, unmodeled thinning of onset abstention beyond the rate arithmetic in threshold_justification, visible in the recorded per-event acting-window records and charged like failure mode 2 if it binds.

Interaction with the recovery branches at B2 and return-A (bounded, recorded): the release gate sits BELOW both recovery branches in the decision order, so it cannot displace a recovery firing; but at states where the graded candidates abstained because recovery was purity-disarmed (the graded purity experiment's additional return-A checkpoint-32 state is one: a purity-disarmed recovery fell through to abstention), this candidate falls through one step further to recent8 when the gate also blocks the abstention - at that graded state recent8 scored 2/14 against the abstention's 0/0 and the ungated recovery's 13/3, so the fall-through can ADD harm at individual late states while removing the abstention from the records. Criterion 5's harm is not directly graded (its successes sub-condition is), but checkpoint-32 successes and harm are reported in full and any such state is named in the report.

Minority-model flip-symmetry limit (carried over, stated): the minority branch this candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (original-segment flip reports reinforce the inverted class in the minority pool). The abstention release gate itself is structure-agnostic (it reads only opposition counts against reference majorities and reference self-agreement), but any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator: release of an ungated abstention branch by reference purity plus acting-window opposition corroboration, not a general excessive-abstention solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_selectivity_restored_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment - the graded abstention-release candidate FAILed it on the development cohort (successes 118 vs recent8 125, required at least 119; the entire deficit one stationary abstention state at control checkpoint 8, seed 392039, surviving both release-gate legs at minimum corroboration - purity 0.857, acting_opposed_count exactly 3) and it is this cycle's selected limitation. Graded per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints), in the identical form carried through the preceding protocols: (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. The realized reference_purity, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, and abstention-gate flags on the control arm are recorded and reported at every checkpoint (design: purity at the pure-segment level 0.8375, leg P armed throughout; leg S is the only leg that can release a stationary abstention), alongside the realized minority_fraction and minority_armed values exactly as in the preceding protocols; the downstream totals are what is graded here, and every control checkpoint at which the raised bar changed the taken branch relative to the records-only abstention-release-rule derivation (the graded candidate's >= 3 rule, see metrics_reported) - in particular every abstention the raised bar blocked that the graded gate would have taken (acting_opposed_count exactly 3 states) and every abstention that survived both legs at the raised bar - is stated explicitly in the report, with the surviving state's purity and support counts named. The graded abstention-release candidate went 16/240 abstentions on development (one surviving state, FAILing this criterion there by 1 success) and 0/240 on additional (PASS, downstream-identical to recent8); this cycle must hold additional AND repair development's failure mode on NEW cohorts, not merely re-draw it.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard - the graded abstention-release candidate PASSed it on both cohorts, including the then-new sub-condition (d) (abstained branch in 0 of 9 states on both cohorts, on additional by actively disarming a late abstention under both legs); all four sub-conditions are carried unchanged in form, and this cycle must not give any of them back while raising the bar. Graded per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive, minority_archive, or abstained) in at most 1 state - the carried records-level release measure for the recovery branches - AND (d) the candidate takes the ABSTAINED branch in 0 of those 9 states (carried from the preceding protocol, where it was new: in the graded purity experiment the additional cohort's single counted state under (c) WAS an abstention, and the graded abstention-release candidate removed abstention from the late records on both cohorts; the raised bar must hold that at zero, not merely at the carried allowance). The realized reference_purity, purity_armed, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, and both abstention-disarmed flags at all 9 states are reported alongside, split by branch taken, so the report distinguishes a gate release of abstention (trigger present, gate blocked it, fell through to recent8 - and by which leg) from a state where no abstention trigger was present at all, and likewise distinguishes the recovery branches' purity releases as in the preceding protocol.

acceptance_criteria.name: second_switch_B2_protection_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged in form from the minority and reference-purity protocols: the raised abstention corroboration bar must not give back the B2 protection the minority branch demonstrated (abstention is not the B2 protective branch - minority recovery is, and it sits above abstention in the decision order - but lost abstention firings at B2 states where neither recovery branch fired return those states to recent8 harm, and that is charged here). Graded per cohort over the B2 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the minority recovery branch is TAKEN (minority_joint_count >= 1, minority branch armed, purity gate armed, acting source minority_archive) in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B2 onset seed-checkpoint states; AND (b) SELECTIVITY - the minority recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 pooled B1 onset states AND at most 1 of the 6 pooled return-A onset states on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B2 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort, AND candidate B2 pooled onset harm <= 0.60 * recent8 B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort; AND (d) PRODUCTIVITY - candidate successes pooled over the B2 onset cells >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16. Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled), with the realized minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, reference_purity, and purity_armed flag at each, and against the records-only minority-rule and reference-purity-rule derivations (see metrics_reported). Abstention-branch firing and abstention-gate disarmings at B2 are reported (with realized acting_opposed_count at each) but do NOT count toward sub-condition (a), as in the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols: per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. The graded abstention-release candidate FAILed it on development (44 vs guard 49 PASS but ceiling 41.4 FAIL by 2.6, identical to its decisive baseline at return-A onset - inherited, not gate-caused) and PASSed it on additional (48 vs guard 66, ceiling 49.2 by 1.2); it is carried unchanged as a co-graded guard: at return-A onset the abstention branch is mostly disarmed by stable disagreement already, so the raised bar's exposure here is small by construction, and any change - or any repeat of the inherited failure - is charged as recorded.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged). Cumulative's, the joint candidate's, the bounded candidate's, the long candidate's, the extended candidate's, the minority candidate's, the reference-purity candidate's, and the abstention-release candidate's return-A successes on the same cohort are reported alongside in full, and any shortfall is stated in the report, not hidden. The release gate (at either bar) sits below both recovery branches and does not enter this criterion's mechanism; it is carried so that any unexpected interaction (for example a fall-through change at a return-A onset state) is graded, not assumed away.

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Carried over unchanged from the graded joint, bounded, long, extended, minority, and reference-purity protocols. The graded abstention-release candidate PASSed it on both cohorts with margins of 30 and 30 harm below the guard (160 vs 190, 6/6 cells; 148 vs 178, 6/6) - those margins are this raised bar's onset budget on comparable cohorts: the hypothesis arithmetic prices the raised bar's ADDITIONAL onset abstention thinning (beyond the >= 3 gate's) at roughly half of the remaining onset firings, each worth roughly 8-15 pooled harm as realized in the preceding cycle, and this criterion grades whether the realized thinning stays inside the margin on NEW cohorts. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record: per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events, acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, support threshold, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity and abstention_disarmed_by_support flags - plus branch taken, recovery-fired flag, minority-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 1(c): candidate B2 pooled onset harm at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's B2 pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's B2 pooled onset harm. Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the guard's pooled onset harm on the same cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. The onset abstention-thinning risk (expected failure mode 2, larger under the raised bar by design) is charged against criteria 1, 3, and 4, not excused from them.
budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 5 and 6 bound abstention's downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144, plus 0 abstained states among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states under criterion 5(d)) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the preceding protocols with this cycle's tightening. Abstention disarmed under stable disagreement is the carried-over release mechanism, not a budget violation; abstention blocked by the release gate at the raised bar is recorded separately (abstention_disarmed_by_purity / abstention_disarmed_by_support) and is likewise not a budget violation - it is this experiment's mechanism, and its onset cost is graded through criteria 1, 3, and 4.

grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary. Criterion 6 is reported first among the criteria in the grading report, as this experiment's primary criterion; criteria 5, 1, and 4 (checkpoint-32 release with its abstention sub-condition, B2 protection, and return-A harm) are reported next, as its co-graded guards.
grading.demonstrated: All seven criteria PASS on BOTH cohorts, the historical transfer benchmark (benchmarks.transfer_benchmark, unchanged) still passes, and the full unit suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests) passes on the evaluation commit.
grading.failed: Criterion 6 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 5 FAILs on the additional cohort, or any of criteria 1, 2, 3, or 4 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 7 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criterion 6 and criterion 7 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 FAILs on either cohort, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only.
grading.regression: The candidate's pooled onset harm exceeds recent8's on both cohorts, or the candidate's stationary-control successes fall below recent8's by more than 6 on both cohorts, or the candidate's checkpoint-32 successes fall below recent8 - 4 on either cohort (the deficit line the graded minority candidate crossed on the additional cohort - 68 vs 82 - and, in the extended protocol's form, the graded extended candidate's worse-cohort deficit line), or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change, plus designer-supplied signal, concordance, minority, routing, expiry, disagreement-age, reference-width, reference-purity, and abstention-release rules at either corroboration bar). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, archive definition, joint tests, minority definition and arming threshold, disagreement / corroboration / long-disagreement conditions, the reference-purity definition and threshold, the acting-window opposition definition and support threshold, and the decision rule are all designer-supplied, and the minority read the candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (see expected failure mode 7). A PASS would demonstrate that a higher corroboration bar on an already-gated abstention branch closes its minimum-corroboration stationary survival without deleting its onset protection - a stationary arm and checkpoint-32 record free of full-refusal states while the onset profile is preserved - in this simulator only, not general excessive-abstention handling, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
grading.ci_claims: Linux/Windows validation is claimed only for an exact commit with a real GitHub Actions run on that commit; otherwise it is recorded as UNVERIFIED.

registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts. No parameter of the twelve graded onset experiments (early_post_switch_adaptation, first_contact_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_retained_recovery, joint_concordance_recovery, bounded_authority_joint_recovery, long_disagreement_joint_recovery, extended_reference_joint_recovery, minority_archive_joint_recovery, reference_purity_gated_recovery, abstention_release_gated_recovery, and the abstention guard counted once) was re-tuned against its inspected cohorts in designing this protocol: the acting model, the extended and legacy references, the retained archive, the archive concordance definition, the joint recovery test's form, the recovery model, the abstention trigger's form and threshold, the local-archive disagreement definition, the corroboration condition, the long-disagreement leg, the minority set definition, the minority concordance and joint tests, the minority arming condition (minority_fraction >= 0.25 with a count floor of 8), the reference-purity definition and threshold (0.70), and the abstention release gate's leg P are reused EXACTLY as frozen in the abstention-release protocol (newest window 2, reference 50 / legacy 24, archive events[:N-26], local window last 26, preceding window 26 before it, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention threshold opposed_count == 2, stable_disagreement iff C >= 1 AND D * 2 > C in both windows, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2, purity threshold 0.70). The single changed element - the abstention release gate's leg S support threshold, acting_opposed_count >= 4 in place of the graded candidate's >= 3 (at least two supporting opposed events beyond the triggering pair, in place of at least one) - is informed only by the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records (their limitation evidence, including the per-state stationary decomposition in limitation_evidence: the surviving state at exactly the old minimum, the blocked state one count below it), the simulator's known noise rates, and this simulator's published segment geometry (240 / 64 / 48 events), never by any score of this experiment (none exist). The >= 4 value was itself pre-computed and publicly priced in the graded abstention-release protocol's threshold justification (checkpoint-2 retention about 0.18) before that experiment was evaluated, so adopting it now is the testing of a pre-registered alternative the preceding cycle deliberately deferred, not a threshold fitted to the inspected 392003-family / 393001-family outcomes.
expected_failure_modes: Stationary false pair surviving BOTH legs at the raised bar (pre-registered, the cycle's central residual risk): leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; the graded abstention-release surviving state realized 0.857) and does not release stationary abstention at all; leg S at >= 4 releases a stationary trigger whenever fewer than 2 of the 6 preceding acting-window events are opposed (probability about 0.75-0.82 per triggered state). A stationary opposed pair WITH two supporting opposed events among the preceding 6 therefore still fires a full 16-task abstention, and a single such state at a control checkpoint where recent8 scores about 10 or more is by itself likely to fail criterion 6's successes sub-condition (margin 6) unless offset by productive control recovery elsewhere, exactly as in the two preceding gradings. This outcome is charged against criterion 6, not excused, and the report must state the surviving state's realized purity, acting_opposed_count, and supporting count.

Onset abstention thinning costing the harm guards (pre-registered, and LARGER than in the preceding cycle by design): the raised bar retains only about 0.39-0.52 of the reference-purity candidate's pooled onset abstentions combined with leg P - the lost firings are concentrated at checkpoint 2 (leg-S retention about 0.18-0.25 there) and at B1 onset, where abstention is the family's only protective response (recovery is archive-discordant-blocked and the minority branch is unarmed there by design). Each lost firing returns 16 tasks to recent8 play at onset harm rates of roughly 8-14 per state; against the graded abstention-release margins (criterion 3: 30 / 30 pooled harm below the guard on its cohorts; criterion 1(c) B2: 40 / 4 below the guard; criterion 4: 5 / 18 below the guard on the (a) comparison) an unlucky cohort - several lost B1 firings, or lost firings concentrated in one cell - can fail criterion 3(a), 1(c), or 4, and that failure is the pre-registered cost side of this cycle's hypothesis, charged, not excused. Realized gate disarmings are recorded at every onset state (split by leg), so a thinning failure is fully distinguishable from a trigger failure in the report. NOTE the asymmetry this creates: the raised bar can convert the preceding cycle's development pattern (one onset disarming, +15 harm, absorbed) into several disarmings whose cost is NOT absorbed - the report must state the realized count of onset disarmings by leg on each cohort.

Criterion 4 failing again on the carried profile, independent of the gate (pre-registered): the graded abstention-release candidate FAILed criterion 4 on development while being identical to its decisive baseline at return-A onset (no onset abstention gate-disarmed there); the return-A harm ceiling is cohort-relative (60 percent of recent8's realized return-A harm), so the same carried profile can miss it on a new cohort with low recent8 return-A harm regardless of what the abstention gate does. Such a failure is charged unchanged and reported as inherited, exactly as in the preceding grading - it neither vindicates nor condemns the raised bar, and the records-only derivations (below) make the attribution checkable.

Late abstention surviving the gate at checkpoint 32 (pre-registered, less likely than in the preceding cycle): leg P's realized checkpoint-32 arming on the graded abstention-release cohorts was 6/9 (development) and 4/9 (additional) states (self-fit compression raised realized purity to 0.613-0.800 against the 0.5675 global design value), so a late state with purity at or above 0.70 AND two supporting opposed events (combined survival about 0.08-0.17 per triggered state) still takes the abstained branch and fails criterion 5's sub-condition (d) (0 of 9 abstained states) even while sub-conditions (a)-(c) pass. That outcome would show even the raised corroboration bar cannot bound the branch's late firing on realized (self-fitted) purity values, and would redirect the next cycle toward an expiry summary that is not self-fitted, under its own new protocol.

Purity leg disarming onset abstention on purity noise (pre-registered, carried over): the checkpoint-4 design purity is 0.8105, about 1.6 sd above the 0.70 threshold at roughly 40 matched reference events, so on an unlucky cohort an onset state can realize purity below 0.70 and lose an abstention firing the reference-purity candidate would have taken; any realized onset purity disarming is recorded and charged against criteria 1, 3, and 4 through the lost protection, compounded with failure mode 2's support-leg thinning.

Support-count span sparsity (pre-registered, carried over, now more binding): the acting-window opposition records score 8 events against reference majorities fitted on about 5-6 events per span; on spans absent from the reference the expectation is null and the event is unmatched (not opposed), so acting_opposed_count can read low on thin-span draws at ANY checkpoint, including genuine onset states - a further, unmodeled thinning of onset abstention beyond the rate arithmetic in threshold_justification, now needing TWO supporting events instead of one, visible in the recorded per-event acting-window records and charged like failure mode 2 if it binds.

Interaction with the recovery branches at B2 and return-A (bounded, recorded, carried over): the release gate sits BELOW both recovery branches in the decision order, so it cannot displace a recovery firing; but at states where the graded candidates abstained because recovery was purity-disarmed, this candidate falls through one step further to recent8 when the gate also blocks the abstention - the fall-through can ADD harm at individual late states while removing the abstention from the records. Criterion 5's harm is not directly graded (its successes sub-condition is), but checkpoint-32 successes and harm are reported in full and any such state is named in the report.

Minority-model flip-symmetry limit (carried over, stated): the minority branch this candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (original-segment flip reports reinforce the inverted class in the minority pool). The abstention release gate itself is structure-agnostic (it reads only opposition counts against reference majorities and reference self-agreement), but any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator: release of an abstention branch by reference purity plus a raised acting-window opposition corroboration bar, not a general excessive-abstention solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
